properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 25 at 4:35PM PST until November 26 at 12:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.5 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory through 4 PM PST Thursday.
For the High Surf Warning, through midnight PST Wednesday
night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW)
at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 3:14PM PST until November 25 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves large
breaking waves up to 25 feet. Surf may worsen coastal flooding
along exposed beaches.. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. Up to 1 foot of saltwater inundation above
ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways.
Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is
predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM PST this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST Thursday.
High tide is at 12:54PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide
gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before
and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this event will be
higher than normal but not quite as high as the previous near
record recording from Tuesday 11/24 at 10.16 feet.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 2:14PM PST until November 26 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. Largest
surf expected on the west side of the islands.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock
damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of
harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of 8.0 feet will peak
between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 2:14PM PST until November 28 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Thursday. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon PST Thursday. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Thursday to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of 7.8 feet will peak
between 9 AM and 11 AM Thursday morning.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

morning's high tide.

* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin
River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and
San Joaquin Counties.


* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 944 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, +2.2
ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.7 ft MHHW
(6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, +2.1
ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.8 ft MHHW
(6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.4 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26, +7.3 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27,
+6.9 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28 and +6.2 ft at 7:00 PM Sun
11/29.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131

tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.
